nodes.body_text: // @vitest-environment jsdom /** * The share panel's DOM half (`createOverlayView`) wired to the real * controller, against a real DOM. * * share-ui.test.mjs drives the controller with a string-capturing view, which * cannot see two things that only exist in a browser: typing reaches the * controller through `input` events (a click on Create does not blur the field * first on touch), and every render replaces the panel's markup, which drops * the focus of a field the member is typing in. This file is identical in * every app that ships src/share.js. */ import { describe, it, expect, vi, afterEach } from "vitest"; import { createShareUi, createOverlayView } from "../src/share.js"; const LATER = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 864e5).toISOString(); afterEach(() => { document.body.innerHTML = ""; document.head.innerHTML = ""; }); describe("share overlay", () => { it("mints with a password typed and never blurred", async () => { const { ui, share } = mount(); await ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); type("hunter22"); document.querySelector('[data-share-action="create"]').click(); await flush(); expect(share.create).toHaveBeenCalledWith("thing", "item-1", expect.objectContaining({ password: "hunter22" })); }); it("keeps focus and the caret in the password field when a render lands mid-typing", async () => { const { ui } = mount(); await ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); type("hun"); const before = field(); await ui.copy("link-1"); // a Copy lands and the panel re-renders expect(field()).not.toBe(before); expect(document.activeElement).toBe(field()); expect(field().value).toBe("hun"); expect([field().selectionStart, field().selectionEnd]).toEqual([3, 3]); }); it("leaves focus off the field while it is disabled for a mint (pins browser behaviour)", async () => { const minting = deferred(); const { ui } = mount({ create: vi.fn(() => minting.promise) }); await ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); type("hunter22"); const creating = ui.create(); expect(field().disabled).toBe(true); expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(field()); minting.resolve({ id: "link-new", url: "https://hub.example/share/new", expiresAt: LATER }); await creating; }); it("restores focus inside the panel even when the host page reuses the id", async () => { const host = document.createElement("input"); host.id = "share-password"; document.body.appendChild(host); const { ui } = mount(); await ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); const inPanel = document.querySelector(".share-panel #share-password"); inPanel.focus(); await ui.copy("link-1"); expect(document.activeElement).toBe(document.querySelector(".share-panel #share-password")); expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(host); }); it("closes on Escape and on a backdrop click", async () => { const { ui } = mount(); await ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "Escape" })); expect(ui.isOpen()).toBe(false); await ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); document.querySelector('[data-testid="share-panel"]').click(); expect(ui.isOpen()).toBe(false); }); });

This file is identical in every app that * ships src/share.js. */ import { describe, it, expect, vi } from "vitest"; import { createShareUi } from "../src/share.js"; /** Same shape as the SDK's activeShareLinks (tested in the hub). */ const ME = { id: "adult-1", name: "Alex" }; const LATER = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 864e5).toISOString(); /** Same shape as the SDK's shareCalendarUrl (tested in the hub). */ describe("share panel", () => { it("lists only live links for the open item, and enables create once the list is read", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [ok([ link(), link({ id: "other", itemId: "item-2", url: "https://hub.example/share/other" }), link({ id: "dead", url: "https://hub.example/share/dead", revokedAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }), ])] }); const opening = h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); expect(h.view.shown).toBe(true); expect(h.view.html).toContain("Checking existing links"); expect(createDisabled(h.view.html)).toBe(true); await opening; expect(h.view.html).toContain("share/abc"); expect(h.view.html).not.toContain("share/other"); expect(h.view.html).not.toContain("share/dead"); expect(createDisabled(h.view.html)).toBe(false); expect(h.view.html).toContain("Only the title and body are shown."); }); it("treats a refused list read as refused, not as no links", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [refused()] }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); expect(h.view.html).toContain('data-testid="share-refused"'); expect(h.view.html).not.toContain('data-testid="share-empty"'); expect(createDisabled(h.view.html)).toBe(true); await h.ui.create(); expect(h.share.create).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("treats a rejected fetch the same as a refusal", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [Promise.reject(new Error("offline"))] }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); expect(h.view.html).toContain('data-testid="share-refused"'); }); it("mints with the item type, id, title and chosen expiry, then copies the url", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [ok([]), ok([link({ id: "link-new", url: "https://hub.example/share/new" })])] }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); h.ui.handleChange({ target: { dataset: { shareAction: "expiry" }, value: "24" } }); await h.ui.create(); expect(h.share.create).toHaveBeenCalledWith("thing", "item-1", { expiresInHours: 24, label: "Wifi" }); expect(h.view.html).toContain("share/new"); expect(h.view.html).toContain("Link created and copied."); expect(createDisabled(h.view.html)).toBe(false); }); it("drops a stale read that lands after a newer one", async () => { const first = deferred(); const second = deferred(); const h = harness({ lists: [first.promise, second.promise] }); const opening = h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); // Reopen on the same item: a new session and a second read. const reopening = h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); second.resolve(ok([link({ url: "https://hub.example/share/fresh" })])); await reopening; first.resolve(ok([])); await opening; expect(h.view.html).toContain("share/fresh"); }); it("shows the minted link when the follow-up read fails", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [ok([]), refused()] }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); await h.ui.create(); expect(h.view.html).toContain("share/new"); expect(h.view.html).toContain("couldn’t be refreshed"); // One blip after a good read is not "sharing is off". expect(h.view.html).not.toContain('data-testid="share-refused"'); }); it("reports a refused mint and re-enables the button", async () => { const h = harness({ create: vi.fn(async () => { throw new Error("Too many active links"); }) }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); await h.ui.create(); expect(h.view.html).toContain("Too many active links"); expect(createDisabled(h.view.html)).toBe(false); }); it("says so when the clipboard write fails after a mint", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [ok([]), ok([link({ id: "link-new", url: "https://hub.example/share/new" })])], writeText: vi.fn(async () => { throw new Error("denied"); }), }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); await h.ui.create(); expect(h.view.html).toContain("Select it above to copy"); }); it("keeps a newer read's list when an older read in the same session lands last", async () => { // Revoke and create both re-read the list. The revoke's read goes out // first but answers last, without the link the create just made. const revokeRead = deferred(); const createRead = deferred(); const h = harness({ lists: [ok([link()]), revokeRead.promise, createRead.promise] }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); const revoking = h.ui.revoke("link-1"); await flush(); const creating = h.ui.create(); await flush(); createRead.resolve(ok([link({ id: "link-new", url: "https://hub.example/share/new" })])); await creating; revokeRead.resolve(ok([])); await revoking; expect(h.view.html).toContain("share/new"); }); it("paints nothing, and leaves the clipboard alone, after the panel closes mid-create", async () => { const minting = deferred(); const writeText = vi.fn(async () => {}); const h = harness({ create: vi.fn(() => minting.promise), writeText }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); const creating = h.ui.create(); h.ui.close(); expect(h.view.shown).toBe(false); minting.resolve({ id: "link-new", url: "https://hub.example/share/new", expiresAt: LATER }); await creating; expect(h.view.html).toBe(""); expect(writeText).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("does not carry one item's result into the next item's panel", async () => { const minting = deferred(); const h = harness({ create: vi.fn(() => minting.promise) }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); const creating = h.ui.create(); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-2", title: "Door code" }); minting.resolve({ id: "link-new", url: "https://hub.example/share/new", expiresAt: LATER }); await creating; expect(h.view.html).toContain("Door code"); expect(h.view.html).not.toContain("Link created"); expect(createDisabled(h.view.html)).toBe(false); }); it("revokes only after confirmation and drops the link even if the re-read fails", async () => { const h = harness({ lists: [ok([link()]), refused()] }); await h.ui.open({ id: "item-1", title: "Wifi" }); await h.ui.revoke("link-1"); expect(h.share.revoke).toHaveBeenCalledWith("link-1"); expect(h.view.html).not.toContain("share/abc"); expect(h.view.html).toContain("Link revoked."); expect(h.share.revoke).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); expect(h.view.html).toContain("share/abc"); }); it("offers revoke on another adult's link only to an admin, and names who made it", async () => { const theirs = link({ createdBy: "adult-2" }); /** The longest any link can last (share-links.ts PREMIUM_MAX_EXPIRY_HOURS). */ const MAX_EXPIRY_HOURS = 8760; const STYLE_ID = "share-ui-style"; const STYLE = ` .share-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; nodes.body_text: function usableItemChoice() { if (!itemChoice || itemChoice.hours > MAX_EXPIRY_HOURS) return null; return entitled || itemChoice.hours <= LAPSED_MAX_EXPIRY_HOURS ? itemChoice : null; }

nodes.body_text: function choices() { const own = usableItemChoice(); const presets = deps.expiryChoices.map(({ hours, label }) => ({ value: String(hours), label, selected: !(own && ownSelected) && hours === expiry, })); return own ? nodes.body_text: function dropItemChoiceIfSelected() { if (ownSelected && !usableItemChoice()) { ownSelected = false; expiry = deps.defaultExpiryHours; } }

nodes.body_text: function itemExpiryChoice(item) { if (!deps.expiryFor) return null; let choice; try { choice = deps.expiryFor(item); } catch { return null; } const hours = Number(choice?.hours); if (!Number.isInteger(hours) || hours <= 0 || !choice?.label) return null; return { hours, label: String(choice.label) }; }

nodes.body_text: async function open(item) { session++; target = { id: String(item.id), title: String(item.title ?? "") }; targetItem = item; links = []; listState = "loading"; busy = false; error = ""; notice = ""; itemChoice = itemExpiryChoice(item); ownSelected = itemChoice !== null; expiry = deps.defaultExpiryHours; password = ""; entitled = false; deps.view.show(); render(); const still = pin(); await refresh(); if (still()) render(); }

nodes.name: create
nodes.body_text: async function create() { if (!target || busy || listState !== "ok") return; const item = target; const secret = password.trim(); // Every reason at once, so fixing one does not uncover the next. const refusals = []; if (writableBlocked()) { refusals.push(`A link that lets visitors ${deps.writableVerb || "respond through the page"} needs an active plan.`); } // The item's own choice is a moment ("the day after the sit ends"), and the // hub counts hours from the mint, so ask again now rather than trusting the // count taken when the panel opened. Gone means the moment has passed. let hours = expiry; if (ownSelected && itemChoice) { const fresh = itemExpiryChoice(targetItem); if (!fresh) { refusals.push(`“${itemChoice.label}” has already passed. Pick how long the link lasts.`); itemChoice = null; ownSelected = false; expiry = deps.defaultExpiryHours; } else if (!entitled && fresh.hours > LAPSED_MAX_EXPIRY_HOURS) { refusals.push(`“${fresh.label}” is more than 30 days away, which needs an active plan. Refuse // rather than mint an open link the member believes is protected. refusals.push("Passwords need an active plan. Clear the password to create an open link."); } else if (password !== "" && secret === "") { refusals.push("A password can’t be only spaces. Clear it for a link with no password."); } else if (secret && secret.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) { refusals.push(`A password needs at least ${MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH} characters.`); } else if (secret.length > MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH) { refusals.push(`A password can be at most ${MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH} characters.`); } if (refusals.length) { notice = ""; error = refusals.join(" "); render(); return; } const still = pin(); busy = true; error = ""; notice = ""; render(); try { const opts = { expiresInHours: hours, label: item.title }; if (secret) opts.password = secret; if (deps.writable) opts.writable = true; const link = await deps.share.create(deps.itemType, item.id, opts); // The field is disabled while the mint is out, so what it holds is what // was sent; clearing it keeps the next link from inheriting the secret. if (still() && password.trim() === secret) password = ""; const listed = await refresh(); if (!still()) return; if (listed === "failed" && !links.some((l) => l.id === link.id)) { // The link exists; only our picture of the list is behind. "Link created and copied." : "Link created. Select it above to copy."; } catch (err) { if (!still()) return; error = err?.message || "Couldn’t create the link."; // The plan lapsed since the list read: show the panel as it is now. if (err?.missingCapability) { entitled = false; dropItemChoiceIfSelected(); } } finally { if (still()) { busy = false; render(); } } }

"Calendar link copied." : "Link copied."; } catch { if (!still()) return; notice = ""; // The calendar link has no field on screen to select, so say it here. error = kind === "calendar" ? `Couldn’t copy. This test is the same check where * it is cheap to fix. */ import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"; import { manifest, prefix, appTableColumns } from "./schema.mjs"; /** Scalar hub-file-id columns. []).includes(column) || manifest.db_encryption === "off", `${table}.${column} would be encrypted at rest`).toBe(true); } } }); });

[]) expect(table, name).toMatch(new RegExp(`\\s${prefix}`)); expect((sql.match(/\?/g) ?? nodes.body_text: /** * Shared migration-schema reader for the manifest ratchets in this suite. * * The manifest names columns the hub resolves in raw SQL — file-reclaim * columns, share-link projections, share-link filters. Every one of those is a * string that no compiler checks, so the tests here re-derive the real column * set from the migrations and compare. */ import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "fs"; import { fileURLToPath } from "url"; import { dirname, join } from "path"; const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); export const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(__dirname, "../manifest.json"), "utf-8")); export const prefix = `app_${manifest.id.replaceAll("-", "_")}__`; const migrationsDir = join(__dirname, "../migrations"); export const schema = readdirSync(migrationsDir) .filter((f) => f.endsWith(".sql")) .sort() .map((f) => readFileSync(join(migrationsDir, f), "utf-8")) .join("\n"); /** Every app table's columns: CREATE TABLE bodies plus appended ALTER TABLE ADD * COLUMN statements. Callers need the ALTERs — several columns arrive in a * later migration than the table. */ /** Columns of one UNPREFIXED table name, as the manifest spells it. */ /** Mirrors the hub's `isPlaintextAppDbColumn`: the only columns a raw-SQL * filter (share-link where/parent_where/order) may name. Note the hub does * NOT consult db_encryption here — an app with encryption off still has to * list a non-conventional column in db_plaintext_columns. */ const BUILTIN_PLAINTEXT = new Set([ "id", "household_id", "created_at", "updated_at", "sent_at", "read_at", "expires_at", "last_synced_at", "completed", "all_day", "status", "type", "category", "week", "emoji", "icon", "position", "sort_order", "pinned", "key", "version", "visibility", "audience", "membership_type", "membership_roles", ]);

nodes.name: createTableBody
nodes.body_text: function createTableBody(table) { const head = new RegExp(`create\\s+table\\s+if\\s+not\\s+exists\\s+["\\[]?${table}["\\]]?\\s*\\(`, "i"); const m = head.exec(schema); if (!m) return null; let depth = 1; let i = m.index + m[0].length; const start = i; while (i < schema.length && depth > 0) { if (schema[i] === "(") depth++; else if (schema[i] === ")") depth--; i++; } return schema.slice(start, i - 1); }

nodes.name: columnNames
nodes.body_text: function columnNames(body) { const segments = []; let depth = 0; let current = ""; for (const ch of body) { if (ch === "(") depth++; else if (ch === ")") depth--; if (ch === "," && depth === 0) { segments.push(current); current = ""; } else current += ch; } segments.push(current); const constraints = new Set(["primary", "unique", "check", "foreign", "constraint"]); return segments .map((s) => s.trim()) .filter(Boolean) .map((s) => s.split(/\s+/)[0].replace(/^["[`]|["\]`]$/g, "")) .filter((name) => !constraints.has(name.toLowerCase())); }

nodes.name: appTableColumns
nodes.body_text: function appTableColumns() { const tables = new Map(); for (const m of schema.matchAll(/create\s+table\s+if\s+not\s+exists\s+["\[]?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)["\]]?\s*\(/gi)) { if (!m[1].startsWith(prefix)) continue; const body = createTableBody(m[1]); if (body) tables.set(m[1], new Set(columnNames(body))); } for (const m of schema.matchAll(/alter\s+table\s+["\[]?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)["\]]?\s+add\s+column\s+["\[]?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)["\]]?/gi)) { tables.get(m[1])?.add(m[2]); } return tables; }

nodes.name: columnsOf
nodes.body_text: function columnsOf(table) { return appTableColumns().get(`${prefix}${table}`); }

nodes.name: isPlaintextColumn
nodes.body_text: function isPlaintextColumn(column) { return BUILTIN_PLAINTEXT.has(column) || column.endsWith("_id") || column.endsWith("_at") || column.endsWith("_date") || column.endsWith("_by") || (manifest.db_plaintext_columns ?? []).includes(column); }

nodes.body_text: #!/usr/bin/env node /** * Build script — reads manifest.json + src/ files (+ migrations/ for storage:"db" * apps) and produces dist/bundle.json. * * dist/bundle.json format: * { * "manifest": { ...AppManifest }, * "migrations": [ { "version": 1, "sql": "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." }, ... ], * "files": { "index.html": "...", "style.css": "..." } * } * * migrations/ naming convention: * 001_init.sql, 002_add_notes.sql — version is the numeric prefix (no leading zeroes in JSON) * * Upload dist/bundle.json as a GitHub release asset. The hub installs it via * POST /api/apps/install with the release asset URL. */ import fs from "fs"; import path from "path"; const ROOT = new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname; const SRC = path.join(ROOT, "src"); const DIST = path.join(ROOT, "dist"); // ── Read manifest ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, "manifest.json"), "utf8")); // ── Read src/ files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const files = readDir(SRC); if (!files["index.html"]) { console.error("Error: src/index.html is required"); process.exit(1); } // ── Validate inline scripts parse ───────────────────────────────────────────── // An app's whole UI is one inline `<script type="module">`, and nothing in the // pipeline parses it: the bundle treats src/ as opaque strings, the hub // validates the manifest rather than the markup, and logic.test.mjs never loads // index.html. A duplicate top-level declaration is a SyntaxError the browser // raises before the first statement runs — the app installs, renders its static // markup, and does nothing (tasks 1.5.1: "Identifier 'dbBatch' has already been // declared"). So every inline script is parsed here, the way the browser will, // and duplicate top-level declarations are named explicitly. { const { execFileSync } = await import("child_process"); const os = await import("os"); const errs = []; const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "inline-scripts-")); let count = 0; try { for (const [name, html] of Object.entries(files)) { if (!name.endsWith(".html")) continue; for (const [, attrs = "", body] of html.matchAll(/<script(\s[^>]*)?>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/g)) { // External scripts and non-JS types (JSON, templates) are not compiled as JS. if (!body.trim() || /\bsrc\s*=/.test(attrs) || /\btype\s*=\s*"(?!module")/.test(attrs)) continue; count++; const isModule = /\btype\s*=\s*"module"/.test(attrs); const file = path.join(dir, `${count}.${isModule ? "mjs" : "cjs"}`); fs.writeFileSync(file, body); try { execFileSync(process.execPath, ["--check", file], { stdio: "pipe" }); } catch (e) { const detail = String(e.stderr ?? e.message).trim().split("\n").filter(Boolean).slice(0, 3).join(" | "); errs.push(`${name}: inline script does not parse — ${detail}`); } const decls = [...body.matchAll(/^(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)|^(?:const|let|class)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)] .map((m) => m[1] ?? m[2]); const seen = new Set(); for (const decl of decls) { if (seen.has(decl)) errs.push(`${name}: top-level "${decl}" is declared more than once`); seen.add(decl); } } } } finally { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); } if (errs.length > 0) { for (const e of errs) console.error(`Error: ${e}`); process.exit(1); } console.log(`Inline scripts: ${count} parsed ✓`); } // ── Read + validate migrations (storage:"db" apps only) ─────────────────────── const MIGRATIONS_DIR = path.join(ROOT, "migrations"); let migrations = []; if (manifest.storage === "db") { if (!fs.existsSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)) { console.error('Error: storage:"db" apps must have a migrations/ directory'); process.exit(1); } const files_ = fs.readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR).filter(f => f.endsWith(".sql")).sort(); if (files_.length === 0) { console.error("Error: migrations/ must contain at least one .sql file"); process.exit(1); } for (const file of files_) { const match = file.match(/^(\d+)/); if (!match) { console.error(`Error: migration file must start with a number: ${file}`); process.exit(1); } const version = parseInt(match[1], 10); const sql = fs.readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file), "utf8").trim(); migrations.push({ version, sql }); } // Validate SQL contracts const FORBIDDEN = [ [/\bdrop\s+table\b/i, "DROP TABLE is not allowed"], [/\bdrop\s+column\b/i, "DROP COLUMN is not allowed"], [/\brename\s+column\b/i, "RENAME COLUMN is not allowed"], [/\balter\s+table\b[^;]+\brename\s+to\b/i, "RENAME TABLE is not allowed"], [/\btruncate\b/i, "TRUNCATE is not allowed"], ]; for (const m of migrations) { for (const [pattern, msg] of FORBIDDEN) { if (pattern.test(m.sql)) { console.error(`Error: migration v${m.version}: ${msg}`); process.exit(1); } } const isCreate = /^\s*create\s+table\b/i.test(m.sql); if (isCreate) { if (!/\bif\s+not\s+exists\b/i.test(m.sql)) { console.error(`Error: migration v${m.version}: CREATE TABLE must use IF NOT EXISTS`); process.exit(1); } } } const versions = migrations.map(m => m.version); if (new Set(versions).size !== versions.length) { console.error("Error: migration versions must be unique"); process.exit(1); } console.log(`Migrations: ${migrations.length} file(s) validated ✓`); } // ── Validate agenda / glance surfaces ───────────────────────────────────────── // The hub re-validates these at publish time and refuses to install a broken // one, so without a local check the first sign of a typo is a failed install // (or, for a display column, a silently dropped widget). These are the // structural rules only — the hub remains the authority. { const errs = surfaceErrors(manifest); if (errs.length > 0) { for (const e of errs) console.error(`Error: ${e}`); process.exit(1); } if (manifest.agenda || manifest.glance) { const which = [manifest.agenda && "agenda", manifest.glance && "glance"].filter(Boolean).join(" + "); console.log(`Surfaces: ${which} validated ✓`); } } // ── Validate inline event handlers resolve to globals ───────────────────────── // An inline `on*=` attribute is compiled by the browser as a function in GLOBAL // scope. Everything declared inside `<script type="module">` is module-scoped, // so such a handler only resolves if the name was explicitly assigned onto // `window`/`globalThis`. Miss one name out of a bridge block and the app builds, // installs, and renders perfectly — then throws // `ReferenceError: Can't find variable: x` the first time a user touches that // one control. Nothing else in the pipeline can see it: the bundle treats src/ // as opaque strings, the hub validates the manifest rather than the markup, and // logic.test.mjs has no DOM. So it is checked here. { const errs = inlineHandlerErrors(files); if (errs.length > 0) { for (const e of errs) console.error(`Error: ${e}`); process.exit(1); } console.log("Inline handlers: all resolve to globals ✓"); } // ── Read scenarios.json (optional per-app behavioral specs) ─────────────────── // Shipped in the bundle so the hub's nightly app-exercise fan-in can replay // scenarios against the published bundle (see hub INTEGRATION_TESTS.md). let scenarios; const SCENARIOS_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "scenarios.json"); if (fs.existsSync(SCENARIOS_FILE)) { scenarios = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(SCENARIOS_FILE, "utf8")); } // ── Read ui-scenarios.json (optional per-app browser specs) ─────────────────── // Layer 3b: Playwright drives the app's own UI inside the real hub. Shipped in // the bundle so the hub can collect scenarios from a published bundle, not just // from a local app dir (see hub DESIGN-app-ui-scenarios.md). let uiScenarios; const UI_SCENARIOS_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "ui-scenarios.json"); if (fs.existsSync(UI_SCENARIOS_FILE)) { uiScenarios = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(UI_SCENARIOS_FILE, "utf8")); } // ── Write bundle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const bundle = { manifest, ...(migrations.length ? { migrations } : {}), files, ...(scenarios ? { scenarios } : {}), ...(uiScenarios ? { ui_scenarios: uiScenarios } : {}), }; fs.mkdirSync(DIST, { recursive: true }); fs.writeFileSync(path.join(DIST, "bundle.json"), JSON.stringify(bundle, null, 2), "utf8"); const totalBytes = Object.values(files).reduce((s, v) => s + v.length, 0); console.log(`Built ${Object.keys(files).length} file(s) — ${(totalBytes / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB → dist/bundle.json`);

nodes.body_text: function surfaceErrors(m) { const errs = []; // Output aliases the query actually produces: every explicit `AS name`, plus // bare selected columns, which are their own alias (`SELECT title` yields // "title", `SELECT b.name` yields "name"). const aliasesOf = (q) => { const out = new Set([...q.matchAll(/\bAS\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)/gi)].map(x => x[1])); const sel = /^\s*SELECT\s+([\s\S]*?)\sFROM\s/i.exec(q); if (sel) { let depth = 0, cur = ""; const items = []; for (const ch of sel[1]) { if (ch === "(") depth++; else if (ch === ")") depth--; if (ch === "," && depth === 0) { items.push(cur); cur = ""; } else cur += ch; } items.push(cur); for (const raw of items) { const t = raw.trim(); if (/\bAS\b/i.test(t)) continue; const bare = /^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\.?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?$/.exec(t); if (bare) out.add(bare[2] ?? bare[1]); } } return out; }; const limitOf = (q) => { const x = /\bLIMIT\s+(\d+)\s*$/i.exec(q.trim()); return x ? parseInt(x[1], 10) : null; }; const checkQuery = (q, where) => { if (typeof q !== "string" || !q.trim()) { errs.push(`${where}.source.query must be a non-empty string`); return false; } if (!/^\s*SELECT\b/i.test(q)) errs.push(`${where}.source.query must be a single SELECT`); if (q.includes(";")) errs.push(`${where}.source.query must not contain a semicolon`); if (/\b(INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|ALTER|CREATE)\b/i.test(q)) errs.push(`${where}.source.query must be read-only`); return true; }; const agenda = m.agenda; if (agenda && agenda.source?.kind === "sql") { const q = agenda.source.query; if (checkQuery(q, "manifest.agenda")) { const aliases = aliasesOf(q); for (const req of ["title", "when_at"]) { if (!aliases.has(req)) errs.push(`manifest.agenda.source.query must select an "${req}" alias`); } const lim = limitOf(q); if (lim === null) errs.push("manifest.agenda.source.query must end with a LIMIT"); else if (lim < 1 || lim > 20) errs.push(`manifest.agenda.source.query LIMIT must be 1-20 (got ${lim})`); // A day token has to narrow the scan, not just be selected or sorted on. // It counts as filtering if it appears anywhere in the WHERE / JOIN ... ON // region, including nested in a function call -- occasions compares // `event_month = CAST(strftime('%m', :today) AS INTEGER)`. const tokens = [...q.matchAll(/:(today|day_start|day_end)\b/g)].map(x => x[0]); if (tokens.length > 0) { const anchor = /\bWHERE\b|\bON\b/i.exec(q); const filterRegion = anchor ? q.slice(anchor.index).replace(/\bORDER\s+BY\b[\s\S]*$/i, "") : ""; if (!tokens.some(t => filterRegion.includes(t))) { errs.push(`manifest.agenda.source.query uses ${tokens[0]} but never filters on it`); } } } } const glance = m.glance; if (glance && glance.source?.kind === "sql") { const q = glance.source.query; if (checkQuery(q, "manifest.glance")) { const aliases = aliasesOf(q); const d = glance.display ?? {}; const TEMPLATES = { stat: ["value"], list: ["title"], badge: ["count"] }; if (!TEMPLATES[d.template]) { errs.push('manifest.glance.display.template must be "stat", "list", or "badge"'); } else { for (const req of TEMPLATES[d.template]) { if (!d[req]) errs.push(`manifest.glance.display.${req} is required for a ${d.template} glance`); } // Every display field names an output alias of the query. for (const f of ["value", "title", "subtitle", "when", "icon", "owner", "count"]) { if (d[f] !== undefined && !aliases.has(d[f])) { errs.push(`manifest.glance.display.${f} "${d[f]}" is not one of the query's selected columns`); } } const lim = limitOf(q); if (d.template === "list" && lim !== null && lim > 5) { errs.push(`manifest.glance.source.query LIMIT must be at most 5 for a list glance (got ${lim})`); } } if (glance.ambient_card !== undefined && glance.ambient_card !== "countdown") { errs.push('manifest.glance.ambient_card must be "countdown"'); } if (glance.ambient_card === "countdown" && d.template !== "list") { errs.push('manifest.glance.ambient_card "countdown" requires display.template "list"'); } } } return errs; }

nodes.body_text: function inlineHandlerErrors(files) { const errs = []; // Names an inline handler may reference without the app declaring them. const AMBIENT = new Set([ "event", "this", "window", "document", "console", "navigator", "location", "history", "alert", "confirm", "prompt", "setTimeout", "setInterval", "clearTimeout", "clearInterval", "fetch", "requestAnimationFrame", "queueMicrotask", "structuredClone", "getComputedStyle", "Number", "String", "Boolean", "Array", "Object", "JSON", "Math", "Date", "RegExp", "Map", "Set", "Promise", "Error", "Symbol", "BigInt", "parseInt", "parseFloat", "isNaN", "isFinite", "encodeURIComponent", "decodeURIComponent", "encodeURI", "decodeURI", // keywords that can precede a `(` and are not calls "if", "for", "while", "switch", "catch", "return", "typeof", "function", "new", "await", "var", ]); // `${...}` is evaluated when the template string is built, in module scope — // it is not part of what the browser compiles as a global handler. const stripInterpolations = (s) => { let out = "", i = 0; while (i < s.length) { if (s[i] === "$" && s[i + 1] === "{") { let depth = 1; i += 2; while (i < s.length && depth > 0) { if (s[i] === "{") depth++; else if (s[i] === "}") depth--; i++; } out += "0"; // placeholder for the interpolated value } else out += s[i++]; } return out; }; // A call can't live inside a string literal (`'var(--accent)'` is not a call). const stripStrings = (s) => s.replace(/'[^']*'/g, "''").replace(/`[^`]*`/g, "``"); // Blank out JS comments so a handler quoted in a comment isn't treated as real // markup. Only whole-line `//` comments, so a `https://` URL survives intact. const stripComments = (js) => js.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "").replace(/^[ \t]*\/\/.*$/gm, ""); for (const [name, html] of Object.entries(files)) { if (!name.endsWith(".html")) continue; const scripts = [...html.matchAll(/<script\b([^>]*)>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/gi)]; const classic = scripts.filter(s => !/type\s*=\s*["']module["']/i.test(s[1])); // What is actually reachable as a global. const globals = new Set(); for (const m of html.matchAll(/\b(?:window|globalThis)\s*\.\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*=(?!=)/g)) { globals.add(m[1]); } // Top-level declarations in a classic (non-module) script really are globals. for (const s of classic) { for (const m of s[2].matchAll(/^(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)) globals.add(m[1]); for (const m of s[2].matchAll(/^(?:var|let|const)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)) globals.add(m[1]); } // Scan handlers in static markup and in rendered template markup alike. let scanned = html; for (const s of scripts) scanned = scanned.replace(s[2], stripComments(s[2])); const seen = new Map(); // missing name -> sample handler for (const m of scanned.matchAll(/\son([a-z]+)\s*=\s*(["'`])([\s\S]*?)\2/gi)) { const body = stripStrings(stripInterpolations(m[3])); for (const c of body.matchAll(/\b([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/g)) { const fn = c[1]; if (AMBIENT.has(fn) || globals.has(fn)) continue; if (c.index > 0 && body[c.index - 1] === ".") continue; // method call if (!seen.has(fn)) seen.set(fn, `on${m[1]}="${m[3].trim().slice(0, 60)}"`); } } for (const [fn, sample] of seen) { errs.push( `${name}: inline handler calls "${fn}()" but nothing assigns window.${fn} ` + `— it is module-scoped, so this throws ReferenceError at click time (${sample})` ); } } return errs; }

nodes.name: dev.mjs
nodes.body_text: #!/usr/bin/env node /** * Generic local dev server for Chickadee Bandit apps. * * Reads the app ID from manifest.json to construct the correct base path. * * hub-sdk.js is fetched from the deployed hub (its canonical source is * packages/hub-contract/src/hub-sdk.js in the hub repo) on first run and cached * locally as .hub-sdk.js (gitignored). If the cache is older than 24 hours * it is refreshed automatically. Falls back to a stale cache when offline. * * Usage: * node dev.mjs # http://localhost:3001 * PORT=3002 node dev.mjs */ import http from "http"; import fs from "fs"; import path from "path"; import https from "https"; import { fileURLToPath } from "url"; const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); const PORT = parseInt(process.env.PORT ?? "3001", 10); const CACHE = path.join(__dirname, ".hub-sdk.js"); const SDK_URL = "https://www.chickadeebandit.com/hub-sdk.js"; const MAX_AGE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 24 hours const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, "manifest.json"), "utf8")); const APP_BASE = `/run/${manifest.id}/`; const MIME = { ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8", ".js": "text/javascript; charset=utf-8", ".css": "text/css; charset=utf-8", ".json": "application/json", ".svg": "image/svg+xml", ".png": "image/png", ".ico": "image/x-icon", }; await ensureSdk(); http.createServer((req, res) => { const url = req.url.split("?")[0]; if (url === "/hub-sdk.js") { serve(res, CACHE); return; } const stripped = url.startsWith(APP_BASE) ? url.slice(APP_BASE.length) : url.replace(/^\//, ""); serve(res, path.join(__dirname, "src", stripped === "" ? "index.html" : stripped)); }).listen(PORT, () => { console.log(`App: ${manifest.name} (${manifest.id})`); console.log(`Dev server: http://localhost:${PORT}`); });

nodes.name: mime
nodes.body_text: function mime(filepath) { return MIME[path.extname(filepath).toLowerCase()] ?? "application/octet-stream"; }

nodes.name: serve
nodes.body_text: function serve(res, filepath) { try { const body = fs.readFileSync(filepath); res.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": mime(filepath) }); res.end(body); } catch { res.writeHead(404, { "Content-Type": "text/plain" }); res.end(`Not found: ${filepath}`); } }

nodes.name: fetchSdk
nodes.body_text: function fetchSdk() { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { https.get(SDK_URL, res => { if (res.statusCode !== 200) { reject(new Error(`HTTP ${res.statusCode}`)); return; } const chunks = []; res.on("data", c => chunks.push(c)); res.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"))); }).on("error", reject); }); }

nodes.name: ensureSdk
nodes.body_text: async function ensureSdk() { const cacheExists = fs.existsSync(CACHE); const cacheAge = cacheExists ? Date.now() - fs.statSync(CACHE).mtimeMs : Infinity; const needsFetch = !cacheExists || cacheAge > MAX_AGE_MS; if (needsFetch) { process.stdout.write(cacheExists ? "Refreshing hub-sdk.js… " : "Fetching hub-sdk.js… "); try { const src = await fetchSdk(); fs.writeFileSync(CACHE, src, "utf8"); console.log("done."); } catch (e) { if (cacheExists) { console.log(`fetch failed (${e.message}), using cached copy.`); } else { console.error(`\nERROR: Could not fetch hub-sdk.js — ${e.message}`); console.error(` Check your internet connection and try again.\n`); process.exit(1); } } } }

nodes.name: logic.js
nodes.body_text: import { isAdult } from "./shared.js"; export { isAdult }; // ── Who may change what ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Mirrors the `owner_or_visibility` row policy every table carries: the member * who added a row may change or delete it, and so may an adult. Everyone may * add. A button this hides is one whose write would do nothing: the hub * answers an UPDATE or DELETE of a row the member may not change with a * success that changed no rows, not with a refusal. */ // ── Tags and locations on an item ──────────────────────────────────────────── /** The ids stored in an item's `tag_ids` / `location_ids` column. */ /** Ids that still name a row. A deleted tag stays in the column until the item * is next saved; it is dropped here so it is never drawn or counted. */ /** A name as two people would agree it is the same one. */ /** The row already carrying this name, so "garage" does not sit beside "Garage". */ // ── Finding items ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Everything a person might type to find an item: its name and note, and the * names of its tags and the places it is stored. `names` maps a tag or * location id to its name. */ /** * Items in a collection that carry EVERY chosen tag and sit in ANY chosen * location. Tags narrow ("Steiff" and "1950s"); an item is only in one place, * so two locations mean "either". */ /** How many items carry each tag or location id. */ // ── Photos ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** An item's photos in the order they are shown: `sort_order`, then oldest first. */ /** The newest item in a collection that has a photo lends the collection its cover. */ // ── Cutouts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * How long a `pending` row is believed. The request is made by the tab that * added the photo; if that tab closed before the answer came back, nothing will * ever write one. Past this the row reads as failed and may be asked for again. */ export const PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; /** * How long a hold this tab has just taken needs no renewing. Nobody else can * take a hold until it is PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS old, so one far younger than that * is still ours, and asking the database to confirm it is a wasted request for * every photo added. A hold that has waited in the queue longer is renewed. */ export const HOLD_FRESH_MS = 60 * 1000; const CUTOUT_STATES = new Set(["none", "pending", "done", "failed", "quota", "unsupported"]); /** * The kinds of picture the hub makes a cutout from. It stores others (a GIF, * and a HEIC kept by an earlier version of the app) and answers a request for * a cutout of one with a 415, every time. */ const CUTOUT_SOURCE_TYPES = /^image\/(jpe?g|png|webp)$/i; /** Whether a cutout can be made from a stored file of this type. A type that * is not known is not ruled out: the hub decides when it is asked. */ /** Where a photo's cutout stands, as the app should treat it right now. */ /** * Whether asking the hub for a cutout is allowed. A photo that has one, or is * waiting for one, is not asked about again: the answer is already here or on * its way, and each ask is a file request against the per-minute limit. */ /** True when the item should be drawn from its cutout, not the photo as taken. */ /** The file to draw. `small` prefers the small copy of whichever picture is * shown: the cutout's own, or the thumbnail of the photo as taken. Never the * one for the other, which is a different picture. */ /** * What a refused cutout request means for the photo's row. * * status what is written to `cutout_status` * stop the hub will refuse every request the same way, so stop asking * for the rest of this visit * message what to tell the person, once * * A 429 is two different refusals. With a `limit` in the reply it is the * household's monthly allowance; without one it is the hub's per-minute limit * on file requests, which a retry a little later gets past. */ /** One line under a photo saying where its cutout stands, or "" when there is nothing to say. */ /** * Whether a cutout the hub has just handed back should be deleted because its * write matched no row. `rowThere` is whether the photo's row was found when * read back (null when that could not be found out) and `named` is the cutout * that row now holds. * * The hub keeps one cutout for a photo and hands the same file to everyone who * asks, so a row that is there and names none may be about to be given this * very file by whoever holds it now. Only a row that is gone, or names another * file, will never name this one. */ /** The most small copies made up for in one visit. */ export const THUMB_BACKFILL_MAX = 40; /** * The photos whose cutout has no small copy and that this member added: the * ones to ask the hub about again, which hands back the cutout it already * holds, at no cost, and lets a small copy be made of it. A small copy is lost * when the request that stores it is refused (a burst of new photos passes the * hub's per-minute limit) or its answer never arrives, and the grid then draws * the cutout whole. `tried` holds the photos already asked about in this * visit, and those this device found to take no copy on an earlier one: one * whose cutout is too small to need a copy is not asked about twice. At most `max`, picked from anywhere in the list so that the same few * do not use up every visit. */ /** The most photos remembered as having a cutout that takes no small copy. */ export const NO_THUMB_MAX = 500; /** * The photos a device remembers as having a cutout that takes no small copy, * with one more: the newest `max`, each once. Such a cutout is small enough * to be its own copy, so asking about it on every visit would fetch it whole * each time for nothing. */ // ── Rows read again ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Rows just read, each as the object already held for it where there is one, * now carrying what was read. A write on its way holds the object of the row * it is changing and sets the outcome on it when the hub answers. Were the * rows read again swapped in as new objects, that outcome would land on one * no longer on show. */ /** * The rows held that a first page read again does not have. They are further * on than a first page reaches, or were deleted on another device, and only * the later pages say which. So they are kept until every page is in: an item * far down a long collection does not vanish, and the sheet open on it does * not close, each time the rows are read again. */ // ── Writes that changed nothing ────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * True when the hub's answer to an UPDATE or DELETE says no row was changed. * That is not a refusal: a row deleted on another device, and a row the member * may not change, both come back as a success with `changed: 0`. An answer * with no count (demo mode) is taken as a write that landed. */ // ── Pictures that did not load ─────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * How long to wait before asking again for a picture that failed to load, or * null once it has been asked for often enough. The hub allows a member a * fixed number of file reads a minute and a long grid scrolled quickly passes * it, so the waits together outlast the minute, and each is spread out so that * a screenful of tiles does not all ask again at the same moment. */ export const IMAGE_RETRY_WAITS_MS = [4_000, 20_000, 60_000]; /** The most statements the hub takes in one batch. */ export const DB_BATCH_MAX = 25; // ── HEIC photos ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** True for a HEIC or HEIF photo, by its type or, when a browser gives it * none, by its name. */ /** * Why a HEIC photo that this browser had already turned into a JPEG was not * added, when the hub refused the JPEG for its size. A JPEG is larger than the * HEIC it was drawn from, so "too large" needs saying in those terms. Null for * any other refusal, which is reported as the hub worded it. */ /** * Why a HEIC photo the hub kept as a HEIC was not added, when the hub's reply * says the JPEG was the trouble: it was too large, or there was no room for * it. Null when the hub could not convert the photo at all, and for a hub * that does not say. */ /** True when the hub kept a picked photo as a HEIC rather than as a JPEG. * `uploaded` is the hub's reply, which names what it stored. A hub that * does not say stored the photo as it was picked. */ // ── The picture a shared page shows ────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Items whose `cover_file_ids` is not what their photos say it should be, with * the value to store: [{ id, value }]. * * A shared collection page shows one picture for each item, and the hub reads * it from that column. It should hold the file the item's tile draws at full * size: its first photo, as the cutout when the item shows one. The hub puts * the photo's own small copy in the tile, so the photo is named, never its * thumbnail. An item with no photo holds an empty list. * * Only call this once every page of `photos` has been read: an item whose * photos have not arrived yet looks like an item with none. */ /** * The cover writes to send, as the batches to send them in: each a list of * { id, value }, none longer than the hub takes in one request. `items` are * the ones this member may change. Empty when every cover is already right. */ // ── Rows deleted while more are still arriving ─────────────────────────────── /** * Rows from a page that arrived late, less the ones deleted in the meantime. * Older items and photos are read behind the first paint, so a page asked for * before a delete can land after it, and adding it whole would bring the * deleted rows back until the next reload. `gone` holds the ids deleted in this * visit: `collections`, `items`, `photos`. A row goes if it was deleted itself * or if the collection or item it belongs to was. */ /** One request for one photo: the row and the stamp of the hold on it. */ /** True when the row itself says a cutout is on its way, whatever its age. */ /** * A `pending` row past its five minutes that the database has not yet been * asked about. Its age alone does not mean it failed: this tab may have been * asleep while another finished the cutout, and what it holds is only its own * old copy. So it is asked about once before it is believed. `checked` holds * the holdKey of every stale request already asked about and found unchanged. */ /** * The photos whose cutout someone else is making, or was: every `pending` row * this tab does not hold that is either still fresh or stale and not yet * checked. Their answer is written by another tab or device, so the only way * to learn it is to ask. At most `max`, the most a batch carries; the stale * ones go first, since they are the ones shown wrongly until asked about. */ // ── Dates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** A date box's value as it is stored: yyyy-mm-dd for a real day, else null. */ /** "12 March 2019" for a stored date, or "" for none. It is a calendar day, * not an instant, so it reads the same in every time zone. */ // ── Small things ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

nodes.body_text: function parseIds(value) { if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.filter((id) => typeof id === "string"); if (typeof value !== "string" || !value) return []; try { const parsed = JSON.parse(value); return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed.filter((id) => typeof id === "string") : []; } catch { return []; } }

nodes.name: toggleId
nodes.body_text: function toggleId(ids, id) { return ids.includes(id) ? ids.filter((other) => other !== id) : [...ids, id]; }

nodes.name: liveIds
nodes.body_text: function liveIds(ids, rows) { const known = new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id)); return ids.filter((id) => known.has(id)); }

nodes.name: nameKey
nodes.body_text: function nameKey(name) { return String(name ?? "").trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ").toLowerCase(); }

nodes.name: findByName
nodes.body_text: function findByName(rows, name) { const key = nameKey(name); return key ? rows.find((row) => nameKey(row.name) === key) ?? null : null; }

nodes.name: tagsOf
nodes.body_text: function tagsOf(tags, collectionId) { return tags.filter((tag) => tag.collection_id === collectionId); }

nodes.name: searchableFields
nodes.body_text: function searchableFields(item, names = new Map()) { const labels = [...parseIds(item.tag_ids), ...parseIds(item.location_ids)] .map((id) => names.get(id)) .filter(Boolean); // The year it was acquired, so "1998" finds everything from that year. const year = cleanDate(item.acquired_date)?.slice(0, 4); return [item.name, item.note, ...labels, ...(year ? [year] : [])]; }

nodes.name: filterItems
nodes.signature: function filterItems(items, { collectionId = null, tagIds = [], locationIds = [] } = {})
nodes.body_text: function filterItems(items, { collectionId = null, tagIds = [], locationIds = [] } = {}) { return items.filter((item) => { if (collectionId && item.collection_id !== collectionId) return false; const tags = parseIds(item.tag_ids); if (!tagIds.every((id) => tags.includes(id))) return false; if (!locationIds.length) return true; const locations = parseIds(item.location_ids); return locationIds.some((id) => locations.includes(id)); }); }

nodes.name: countByLabel
nodes.body_text: function countByLabel(items, column) { const counts = new Map(); for (const item of items) { for (const id of parseIds(item[column])) counts.set(id, (counts.get(id) ?? 0) + 1); } return counts; }

nodes.name: photosOf
nodes.body_text: function photosOf(photos, itemId) { return photos .filter((photo) => photo.item_id === itemId) .sort((a, b) => (a.sort_order - b.sort_order) || String(a.created_at).localeCompare(String(b.created_at)) || String(a.id).localeCompare(String(b.id))); }

nodes.name: coverPhoto
nodes.body_text: function coverPhoto(photos, itemId) { return photosOf(photos, itemId)[0] ?? null; }

nodes.name: collectionCover
nodes.body_text: function collectionCover(items, photos, collectionId) { const withPhotos = new Set(photos.map((photo) => photo.item_id)); const item = items.find((candidate) => candidate.collection_id === collectionId && withPhotos.has(candidate.id)); return item ? coverPhoto(photos, item.id) : null; }

nodes.name: holdIsFresh
nodes.body_text: function holdIsFresh(stamp, now = Date.now()) { const taken = Date.parse(stamp ?? ""); return Number.isFinite(taken) && now - taken >= 0 && now - taken < HOLD_FRESH_MS; }

nodes.name: cutoutSupported
nodes.body_text: function cutoutSupported(mimeType) { return !mimeType || CUTOUT_SOURCE_TYPES.test(mimeType); }

nodes.name: cutoutState
nodes.body_text: function cutoutState(photo, now = Date.now()) { if (photo.cutout_file_id) return "done"; const status = CUTOUT_STATES.has(photo.cutout_status) ? photo.cutout_status : "none"; // "done" with no file is a row whose cutout was reclaimed or never written. if (status === "done") return "failed"; if (status !== "pending") return status; const asked = Date.parse(photo.cutout_requested_at ?? ""); return Number.isFinite(asked) && now - asked < PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS ? "pending" : "failed"; }

nodes.name: canRequestCutout
nodes.body_text: function canRequestCutout(photo, now = Date.now()) { const state = cutoutState(photo, now); return state === "none" || state === "failed" || state === "quota"; }

nodes.name: showsCutout
nodes.body_text: function showsCutout(photo) { return !!photo.cutout_file_id && Number(photo.use_cutout) !== 0; }

nodes.name: displayFileId
nodes.body_text: function displayFileId(photo, { small = false } = {}) { if (showsCutout(photo)) return (small && photo.cutout_thumb_file_id) || photo.cutout_file_id; return (small && photo.thumb_file_id) || photo.file_id; }

nodes.name: cutoutFailure
nodes.body_text: function cutoutFailure(status, detail = null) { if (status === 429 && typeof detail?.limit === "number") { return { status: "quota", stop: true, message: `This month's ${detail.limit} photo cutouts are used up. New photos are kept as taken.` }; } if (status === 429) return { status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }; if (status === 402) { return { status: "none", stop: true, message: "Removing photo backgrounds needs an active plan. Photos are kept as taken." }; } if (status === 403) return { status: "none", stop: true, message: "" }; if (status === 503) { return { status: "failed", stop: true, message: "Removing photo backgrounds is unavailable right now. Photos are kept as taken; try again later." }; } if (status === 413) return { status: "failed", stop: false, message: "That photo is too large to remove the background from." }; // Not this request's bad luck but the picture's kind: asking again is // refused again, so the row says so and is never asked about after. if (status === 415) { return { status: "unsupported", stop: false, message: "The background can be removed from JPEG, PNG and WebP photos only." }; } // Every cutout after this one would be refused for the same reason. if (status === 507) { return { status: "failed", stop: true, message: "There is no storage left for photos with the background removed. Photos are kept as taken." }; } return { status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }; }

nodes.name: cutoutLabel
nodes.body_text: function cutoutLabel(state) { switch (state) { case "pending": return "Removing the background…"; case "failed": return "The background could not be removed."; case "quota": return "This month's cutouts are used up."; case "unsupported": return "The background cannot be removed from this kind of picture."; default: return ""; } }

nodes.name: cutoutIsUnnamed
nodes.body_text: function cutoutIsUnnamed(rowThere, named, madeId) { if (rowThere === null || rowThere === undefined) return false; if (!rowThere) return true; return !!named && named !== madeId; }

nodes.name: missingCutoutThumbs
nodes.signature: function missingCutoutThumbs(photos, me, tried = new Set(), max = THUMB_BACKFILL_MAX, random = Math.random)
nodes.body_text: function missingCutoutThumbs(photos, me, tried = new Set(), max = THUMB_BACKFILL_MAX, random = Math.random) { if (!me) return []; const missing = photos.filter((photo) => photo.cutout_file_id && !photo.cutout_thumb_file_id && photo.created_by === me.id && !tried.has(photo.id)); if (missing.length <= max) return missing; const start = Math.floor(random() * missing.length); return [...missing.slice(start), ...missing.slice(0, start)].slice(0, max); }

nodes.name: withNoThumb
nodes.body_text: function withNoThumb(remembered, id, max = NO_THUMB_MAX) { return [...remembered.filter((held) => held !== id), id].slice(-max); }

nodes.name: intoHeld
nodes.body_text: function intoHeld(held, read) { const known = new Map(held.map((row) => [row.id, row])); return read.map((row) => { const mine = known.get(row.id); return mine ? Object.assign(mine, row) : row; }); }

nodes.name: carriedOver
nodes.body_text: function carriedOver(held, read) { const got = new Set(read.map((row) => row.id)); return held.filter((row) => !got.has(row.id)); }

nodes.name: wroteNothing
nodes.body_text: function wroteNothing(result) { return result?.changed === 0; }

nodes.name: imageRetryDelay
nodes.body_text: function imageRetryDelay(tries, random = Math.random) { const wait = IMAGE_RETRY_WAITS_MS[tries]; return wait === undefined ? null : Math.round(wait * (1 + random() / 2)); }

nodes.name: isHeic
nodes.body_text: function isHeic(file) { // `.hif` is the same format under the name some cameras give it. return /^image\/hei[cf]/i.test(file?.type ?? "") || /\.(hei[cf]|hif)$/i.test(file?.name ?? ""); }

nodes.name: heicRefusal
nodes.body_text: function heicRefusal(name, status) { if (status === 413) return `"${name}" is too large to add: a HEIC photo is stored as a JPEG, which is the larger of the two.`; if (status === 507) return `There is no storage left for "${name}": a HEIC photo is stored as a JPEG, which is the larger of the two.`; return null; }

nodes.name: heicKeptRefusal
nodes.body_text: function heicKeptRefusal(name, uploaded) { return heicRefusal(name, { too_large: 413, no_room: 507 }[uploaded?.notConverted]); }

nodes.name: storedAsHeic
nodes.body_text: function storedAsHeic(uploaded, picked) { return isHeic({ type: uploaded?.mimeType ?? picked?.type, name: uploaded?.name ?? picked?.name }); }

nodes.name: staleCovers
nodes.body_text: function staleCovers(items, photos) { const first = new Map(); for (const photo of photos) { const best = first.get(photo.item_id); if (!best || photosOf([best, photo], photo.item_id)[0] === photo) first.set(photo.item_id, photo); } const stale = []; for (const item of items) { const cover = first.get(item.id); const want = cover ? [displayFileId(cover)] : []; const have = parseIds(item.cover_file_ids); if (have.length !== want.length || have[0] !== want[0]) stale.push({ id: item.id, value: JSON.stringify(want) }); } return stale; }

nodes.name: coverWrites
nodes.body_text: function coverWrites(items, photos, max = DB_BATCH_MAX) { const stale = staleCovers(items, photos); const batches = []; for (let i = 0; i < stale.length; i += max) batches.push(stale.slice(i, i + max)); return batches; }

nodes.name: withoutDeleted
nodes.body_text: function withoutDeleted(rows, gone) { return rows.filter((row) => !gone.items.has(row.id) && !gone.photos.has(row.id) && !gone.collections.has(row.collection_id) && !gone.items.has(row.item_id)); }

nodes.name: holdKey
nodes.body_text: function holdKey(photo) { return `${photo.id}|${photo.cutout_requested_at ?? ""}`; }

nodes.name: unresolved
nodes.body_text: function unresolved(photo) { return !photo.cutout_file_id && photo.cutout_status === "pending"; }

nodes.name: needsCheck
nodes.signature: function needsCheck(photo, heldHere, checked, now = Date.now())
nodes.body_text: function needsCheck(photo, heldHere, checked, now = Date.now()) { return unresolved(photo) && !heldHere.has(photo.id) && cutoutState(photo, now) !== "pending" && !checked.has(holdKey(photo)); }

nodes.name: pendingElsewhere
nodes.signature: function pendingElsewhere(photos, heldHere, checked = new Set(), now = Date.now(), max = DB_BATCH_MAX)
nodes.body_text: function pendingElsewhere(photos, heldHere, checked = new Set(), now = Date.now(), max = DB_BATCH_MAX) { const stale = photos.filter((photo) => needsCheck(photo, heldHere, checked, now)); const fresh = photos.filter((photo) => unresolved(photo) && !heldHere.has(photo.id) && cutoutState(photo, now) === "pending"); return [...stale, ...fresh].slice(0, max); }

nodes.name: cleanDate
nodes.body_text: function cleanDate(value) { const text = String(value ?? "").trim(); const match = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(text); if (!match) return null; const [year, month, day] = match.slice(1).map(Number); const date = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day)); // Date rolls 31 February over into March; a day that does not exist is not stored. return date.getUTCFullYear() === year && date.getUTCMonth() === month - 1 && date.getUTCDate() === day ? text : null; }

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.body_text: function formatDate(value, locale = undefined) { const clean = cleanDate(value); if (!clean) return ""; const [year, month, day] = clean.split("-").map(Number); return new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day)) .toLocaleDateString(locale, { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric", timeZone: "UTC" }); }

nodes.name: plural
nodes.body_text: function plural(count, one, many = `${one}s`) { return `${count} ${count === 1 ? one : many}`; }

nodes.name: reads.js
nodes.body_text: // Every SELECT the app sends. The first-render ones are also declared in // manifest.preload, which the hub answers from rows embedded in the document; // __tests__/preload.test.mjs holds the two copies together. /** * Items and photos are read a page at a time, newest first, and the two page * sizes answer to different limits. * * The FIRST page of each is preloaded: the hub embeds the rows in the document * and the app's first request costs nothing. The hub drops a whole preload over * 256 KB, and a photo row is about 500 bytes of JSON and an item row about 420 * before its note, so the first page is small enough that both fit with room * for notes, collections, tags and places. * * Every LATER page travels over the network, where the hub refuses a reply of * more than 2 MB (and of more than 5,000 rows). The size is the one that * binds: an item's note may run to 2,000 characters, which can be 6,000 bytes, * so a round of 200 items and 200 photos stays under it even when every note * is full. A larger page would be fewer requests for most households and a * request that fails on every launch for one with long notes, with nothing * after the first page ever shown. */ export const FIRST_PAGE_SIZE = 110; export const NEXT_PAGE_SIZE = 200; export const READS = { collections: "SELECT id, name, description, auto_cutout, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_collections__collections ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC", tags: "SELECT id, collection_id, name, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__tags ORDER BY created_at, id", locations: "SELECT id, name, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__locations ORDER BY created_at, id", items: `SELECT id, collection_id, name, note, acquired_date, tag_ids, location_ids, cover_file_ids, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_collections__items ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${FIRST_PAGE_SIZE}`, photos: `SELECT id, collection_id, item_id, file_id, thumb_file_id, cutout_file_id, cutout_thumb_file_id, cutout_status, cutout_requested_at, use_cutout, sort_order, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__photos ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${FIRST_PAGE_SIZE}`, }; /** The order of the first-render batch, and of manifest.preload. */ export const READ_ORDER = ["collections", "tags", "locations", "items", "photos"]; // The page after a given row. Same columns and order as the first page, so the // pages concatenate. export const NEXT_PAGE = { items: `SELECT id, collection_id, name, note, acquired_date, tag_ids, location_ids, cover_file_ids, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_collections__items WHERE (created_at < ? OR (created_at = ? AND id < ?)) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${NEXT_PAGE_SIZE}`, photos: `SELECT id, collection_id, item_id, file_id, thumb_file_id, cutout_file_id, cutout_thumb_file_id, cutout_status, cutout_requested_at, use_cutout, sort_order, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__photos WHERE (created_at < ? OR (created_at = ? AND id < ?)) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${NEXT_PAGE_SIZE}`, }; /** Batch results keyed by read name. A missing result reads as no rows. */ /** * The statements for the next round of pages, given the last page read of each * table and the size that page was asked for. Both tables go in one batch, so * a round is one request however many tables still have rows to come. Empty * when everything has been read. */ /** Params for NEXT_PAGE, or null when `rows`, asked for `pageSize` at a time, was the last page. */

nodes.name: firstRenderBatch
nodes.body_text: function firstRenderBatch() { return READ_ORDER.map((name) => ({ sql: READS[name] })); }

nodes.name: namedResults
nodes.body_text: function namedResults(results) { const named = {}; READ_ORDER.forEach((name, i) => { named[name] = results?.[i]?.rows ?? []; }); return named; }

nodes.name: nextPageBatch
nodes.body_text: function nextPageBatch(lastPages, pageSize) { return Object.keys(NEXT_PAGE) .map((name) => ({ name, sql: NEXT_PAGE[name], params: nextPageParams(lastPages[name] ?? [], pageSize) })) .filter((statement) => statement.params); }

nodes.name: nextPageParams
nodes.body_text: function nextPageParams(rows, pageSize) { if (!rows.length || rows.length < pageSize) return null; const last = rows[rows.length - 1]; return [last.created_at, last.created_at, last.id]; }
